chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismāʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: “A group of people dug a pit for a lion in Yemen, and the lion fell into it.

There was the lion, so the people crowded around it, looking at the lion. Then a man fell, and he clung to another, and the other clung to another, and another to another, and the lion wounded them. Among them were those who died from the lion’s wounds, and among them were those who were brought out and then died. They disputed over that until they took up swords.

Then Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام said, “Come, I will judge between you.” So he ruled that “the first is entitled to one-quarter of the blood-money, the second to one-third of the blood-money, the third to one-half of the blood-money, and the fourth to the full blood-money.” And he placed that liability upon the tribes of those who had crowded together.

So some of the people were satisfied and some were displeased. Then that was referred to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he was informed of the judgment of Ali, Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام, and he approved it.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-money paid as legal compensation for death
key_terms.زُبْيَةَ: a pit dug as a trap, here for the lion
key_terms.فَأَجَازَهُ: he approved and ratified the judgment
key_terms.قَبَائِلِ: the tribes upon whom liability was assigned

ai.seo_question: How did Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام rule on shared liability when several people died in a crowding incident?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a case of accidental collective harm arising from a crowd gathering around a trapped lion, leading to multiple deaths. Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام apportioned the diyah according to the degree of causal involvement, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم approved his judgment. The report is significant in jurisprudence for shared liability in jinayat cases.
